Organize your ideas clearly and support them with details from the text. : Make sure your response includes the following : Introduction with a strong thesis, 3 body paragraphs with topic sentences, and a conclusion (5 points) Write 5 clear paragraphs : Support each point with facts or example
questions.student_answer:
The solar panel project greatly improved the village's energy supply and habits.




For years the families had used kerosene lamps and candles for light, but the solar panels changed everything. Solar panels use solar energy, the sun's rays, and turns them into electricity that people can use. So, a community-led project, funded by a mix of donations and government support, brought rows of solar panels to everyones houses.




With the expansion of solar panels, the village children could stay up late in the evenings to study. Many other businesses benefited from the solar panels, including the shops, being able to stay open later, boosting local business. Even the small medical clinic, which once closed at sunset, could now store vaccines and operate equipment all night long.




The changes could not come without challenges though. A handful of the residents worried that the cost of keeping the solar panels would be too much. And others feared that the tech might fail during a cloudy week. After some time, the project leaders organized workshops on panel care and energy-saving habits that, over time, built both knowledge and trust.




Even today, the village stands as a model for other small communities seeking cheap, renewable energy sources.

questions.prompt: Read the passage . The Robotics Club That Changed a School Write an  explaining . expository essay how the robotics club changed Lincoln Middle School and its students Use information from the passage to describe at least . Organize your ideas clearly and support them with details from the text. three ways the club made a difference : Make sure your response includes the following : Introduction with a strong thesis, 3 body paragraphs with topic sentences, and a conclusion (5 points) Write 5 cle
questions.student_answer:
The robotics club changed Lincoln Middle School and its students forever by helping students think through problems better, and being patient when working through problems.

The club started small, but that did not stop them from forming a team and going to a regional competition for robotics. On the first day, only eight students had signed up. The club met in a small storage room with only some small kits people had borrowed. Soon, however, the club was buzzing with energy. The advent of the robotics club had been marked, and would not soon be forgotton.

After some consideration, the first 'challenge' was building a robot that could pick up and hold small items. The students worked in pairs testing sensors, motors, and more. They often failed, then tried again. A real engineer, that was retired, offered to help, teaching how to deal with problems like they were real inventors. By spring, the team enetered a regional competition, did not win, but got awarded for teamwork. More importantly, they came home with ideas and confidence.

Over time, the club had started changing the students, and more students were signing up for it. After the word spread, that following year, forty students applied to join the club! The school also noticed a change in the students who where a part in it. They reported the club members asking more questions in science, and showing more patience when dealing with problems. With enough time, the principal approved a bigger space and funding for the new equipment for the club.

Even up to today, the robotics club is of the most popular clubs in Lincoln Middle School. In addition, the former members went on to study engineering and computer science. Those eight interested students and a borrowed kit will never be forgotton, because of the tradition that continues to this day.

questions.student_answer:
The story of Michaela Benthaus's journey to space shows that determiation and technology can break barriers.

When Michaela was a kid, she dreamed of becoming an astronaut. Sadly, in 2018, she hurt her spine in a bike accident that left her in a wheelchair! Nevertheless, she kept studying engineering, and eventually joined a training program with the European Space Agency in 2024. Michaela's dream was getting closer by the day.

The agency was going to take a trip to space, and to aid them, Michaela reached out to a couple of helpers. First, she talked to Hans Keonigsmann, a retired rocket engineer. Then, with his help, they asked Blue Origin for assistance. The company agreed and spent months working with Michaela to plan every detail of the trip.

The process of getting the flight ready took some time. First, they added a platform that allowed Michaela to slide from her wheelchair into a seat. Then, a special strap that held her legs in place so they would not drift while floating. Finally, they adjusted the seat so it could support her body during the strong forces of the liftoff and landing. Along with these changes came the idea that with careful planning, rockets could be made for anyone.

Michaela's flight has not only sparked bigger plans for making space more open, but it also counts as proof that the sky is not a limit anymore. Additionally, the European Space Agency has approved John McFall, a runner with an artificial leg, for a future trip to the International Space Station.

Today, I will tell you about the language El Silbo. Where it was spoken, how and why it was spoken, and how the language almost was forgotten.







El Silbo, a language found just off the coast of Africa. A group of islanders known for their steep valleys and cliffs. Visitors of the island often came to hear the amazing sounds of the birds. It was called El Silbo Gomero, or the Whistle of Gomera and it is spoken from only tones. Now, no one actually knows where the language orginated. However, people belived that the language was adopted by Spanish settlers around the 1500s. 




For many years, the settlers used the whistled language to communicate across the island's landscape. Every consonant and vowel is replaced with a whistle of different length or pitch. The sounds from the whistle can travel almost 2 miles, more than any talking or shouting could do. Message whisped from hill to hill. Whether it be invitations, news, or warnings. Before modern cell phones or ipads, ElSilbo was a necessity rather than a made up language.




Unfortunely, around the 1980s not many people remembered the language and it was almost forgotten. However, the government soon recognized the risk of losing an important part of the island's identity and history. In an effort to fix this, the government made it required that schools must have classes that teach El Silbo. Today, every student learns about El Silbo, though adults just use it to host events or entertain tourists. Even now we still have a new generation of islanders. For example, Cyro he is a young whistler and takes pride with keeping El Silbo alive, carrying the voice of their ancestors through the moutain breeze.







Now you know where it was spokeb, how and why it was spoken, and how the language was almost forgotten. I suggest you go tell someone about El Silbo or do some research yourself because it is an amazing language.

questions.student_answer: Monarch butterflies are amazing creatures that fly from Canada and the U.S. to migrate to the forests of Mexico for the winter. However, recently, fewer monarchs have been making the perilous journey to the forests of Mexico. As a result, people around the U.S. have been making an effort to make way stations for butterflies to rest during their journey. While the butterflies are at the way stations, people study and tag them and send the data to scientists so they can track the monarchs' migration patterns. Because of these way stations and citizen scientists, more monarchs have survived the journey to the forests of Mexico. In conclusion, monarch butterflies are amazing creatures that migrate from around the world to get to the warm forests of Mexico to reproduce and rest during the winter season. People have helped these monarchs get to their destination safe and sound.

questions.prompt: Write an  explaining how students learn new languages in effective ways. expository essay  Use information from the passage to support your ideas.   : Make sure your response includes the following  : Introduction with a strong thesis, 3 body paragraphs with topic sentences, and a conclusion (5 points) Write 5 clear paragraphs   : Support each point with facts or examples from the passage and explain what they show (5 points) Use evidence and explain it   : Use transitions, keep your ideas in or
questions.student_answer: In a busy neighborhood café, people speak many different languages. A family at one table talks in Spanish. At the counter, a worker sings along to a French song on the radio. Scenes like this happen across the United States, a country shaped by immigrants. Even though English is the most common school language, many Americans grow up using two languages at home and in their communities. Learning multiple languages can help people in many different ways. Studies show it can help with memorization and improve resilience and problem-solving skills. Studies also show that infants and younger kids learn faster and have an easier time using proper pronunciation. As a result, many families have started teaching kids second languages while they are infants. One of many ways children can learn is through immersion. Immersion is a class where the teachers use the language during all parts of the day, from simple conversation to learning new subjects. Using the immersion method can help kids hear the language and figure out the vocabulary. One other helpful method uses real communication. Some classrooms connect students with pen pals across the globe. When students reach out to them, they create a bond. This bond can help kids find motivation to learn their language to understand the culture of their pen pal. In conclusion, learning a second language is important for understanding immigrants and peers. Learning a new language can help a child grow their brain and understand others' culture. Languages can be taught in multiple different ways, including immersion and talking to pen pals. Children can also be taught at a young age to make pronunciation easier. Languages have many purposes in a child's brain, but the main reason is to help others share culture and feel welcome.

incorrect_questions.prompt: Write an  explaining how students learn new languages in effective ways. expository essay  Use information from the passage to support your ideas.   : Make sure your response includes the following  : Introduction with a strong thesis, 3 body paragraphs with topic sentences, and a conclusion (5 points) Write 5 clear paragraphs   : Support each point with facts or examples from the passage and explain what they show (5 points) Use evidence and explain it   : Use transitions, keep your ideas in or
incorrect_questions.student_answer: In a busy neighborhood café, people speak many different languages. A family at one table talks in Spanish. At the counter, a worker sings along to a French song on the radio. Scenes like this happen across the United States, a country shaped by immigrants. Even though English is the most common school language, many Americans grow up using two languages at home and in their communities. Learning multiple languages can help people in many different ways. Studies show it can help with memorization and improve resilience and problem-solving skills. Studies also show that infants and younger kids learn faster and have an easier time using proper pronunciation. As a result, many families have started teaching kids second languages while they are infants. One of many ways children can learn is through immersion. Immersion is a class where the teachers use the language during all parts of the day, from simple conversation to learning new subjects. Using the immersion method can help kids hear the language and figure out the vocabulary. One other helpful method uses real communication. Some classrooms connect students with pen pals across the globe. When students reach out to them, they create a bond. This bond can help kids find motivation to learn their language to understand the culture of their pen pal. In conclusion, learning a second language is important for understanding immigrants and peers. Learning a new language can help a child grow their brain and understand others' culture. Languages can be taught in multiple different ways, including immersion and talking to pen pals. Children can also be taught at a young age to make pronunciation easier. Languages have many purposes in a child's brain, but the main reason is to help others share culture and feel welcome.

skills.skill: Identify Topic Sentence And Sequence Details

analysis.pattern_summary: Jagger shows consistent struggles with sentence construction mechanics, particularly appositives, fragments, and logical conjunctions. Despite showing good paragraph development skills in longer responses, he fails on targeted grammar and sentence-level tasks that require precise understanding of sentence structure and grammatical rules.
analysis.skill_gaps: appositive construction, fragment identification and correction, subject-verb agreement, conjunction usage, spelling accuracy, logical sentence combining
analysis.alphawrite_vs_test: The AlphaWrite data shows all skills marked as "MASTERED" with "None%" scores, indicating a significant disconnect between the skill tracking system and actual performance on standardized tests. This suggests either incomplete practice or inaccurate mastery assessment.
analysis.rushing_impact: Rushing on 3 out of 4 tests likely contributed significantly to mechanical errors and incomplete sentence construction, though underlying skill gaps would persist regardless.
analysis.recommended_activities:
- Write Appositives (Sentences G4): student consistently fails appositive construction questions scoring 0-50%
- Fragment Or Sentence (Sentences G4): needs reinforcement despite "mastered" status given continued fragment errors
- Combine Sentences (Sentences G4): struggles with logical conjunction usage and sentence flow
- Subject Verb Agreement (Sentences G3): errors like "petals are" instead of "petals is" indicate basic agreement issues
- Spelling and Mechanics (Writing Foundations G4): consistent spelling errors affecting overall writing quality

questions.title: Essay with Rich Text
questions.prompt: Write an  explaining how the solar panel project improved life in the village. expository essay Use information from the passage to describe at least three different ways the project changed the community. Organize your ideas clearly and support them with details from the text. : Make sure your response includes the following : Introduction with a strong thesis, 3 body paragraphs with topic sentences, and a conclusion (5 points) Write 5 clear paragraphs : Support each point with facts or example
questions.student_answer:
Solar power, a new inovative technology that captures the energy from the sun, has now been set up in a off the grid rural town. This town previously had not had electricity but community led projects pushed for widespread solar panel setup on all the residents roofs. Before these solar panels were installed the town had to run by candles and fire for illumination. These solar panels changed how the town functioned, now shops could stay open later, and the clinic could store medicine over night. This tranformation has inspired other towns with similar situations to consider the solar panel concept.




	Before the solar panels were installed, the town was dark at night, and kids and buissneses had to close early or function by firelight. During the night the town was dark and hospitals could not function or keep medicne over night because of lack of electricity. The community members discovered solar panels and thought it was a good fit for the community. One of the biggest problems that is stated in the story in paragraph 2, "Even the small medical clinic, which once closed at sunset, could store vaccines and operate equipment at night." That qoute shows one of the biggest probems that a lack of power presents, and the new solar panels solved this problem.




	Once the panels were insltaled, people were curious about how to take care of them and keep them running. The community started to run workshops to teach the towns families how to clean, maintain and understand the power from the solar panels.  In the 3rd paragraph of the story they state, "However, the transformation was not without challenges...project leaders organized workshops on panel care and energy saving habits." In this quote it shows how the residents were concered but with these frequent workshops all their questions and concerns were solved.




	The town has now become a model for sustainable living as it uses renuable energy for all of the towns needs. The residents take pride in their solar panel setups, and how they were one of the first to adpot the technology. In the last paragraph of the story they say, "The shift to solar energy not only improved daily life-it also strengthened the spirt of cooperation among neighbors." In that sentence they say how it also stregthed the community bond beacuse they all participated in a large pionering project that broght them together. The town has benifited in more ways than just improving their own life, but inspiring and bringing others toghther.




	In conclusion, this town has evolved from candlelight to inspiring people to set up solar for themselves. They now have power at night for the residents, stores, and hospitals so they can open and stay up after dark. This large transformative project has broght the town community closer. Finaly, this solar project improved this small village by a large amount and a story for others to get inspired.

questions.title: Essay with Rich Text
questions.prompt: Write an  explaining how the bike lane project improved life in the town. expository essay Use information from the passage to describe at least three ways the project changed the community (e.g., safety, business, family travel). Organize your ideas clearly and support them with details from the text. : Make sure your response includes the following : Introduction with a strong thesis, 3 body paragraphs with topic sentences, and a conclusion (5 points) Write 5 clear paragraphs : Support each po
questions.student_answer:
You have probably seen a bike lane, but this town had never and it just happend to change their whole community. This town decided to add bike lanes after people felt unsafe riding or walking. When the new bike lanes were added the drivers slowed and there was more foot traffic. Shops and schools saw more people walking or riding to get places and parents said they felt calmer knowing that their kids were safe. This small change turned the community around making the streets slower and giving more space for pedestrians and bikers.




	At first, these streets were busy beacuse people were driving instead of walking everywhere. Once the bike lanes were installed the streets shrunk and more people were encoraged to walk and bike. In the second paragraph of the story they say, "Students could bike to school without hugging the curb." This shows an example of how people can commute safely to and from school. This can go back to the idea that this town had a community upgrade beacuse you start seeing more faces on the street.




	At first shops and local buissnes started to get more people passing by their stores before and after work. You may ask why and that beacuse the paths people commuted on were passing these local shops. This caused them to open longer hours so they could accomodate the influx in customers. In paragraph two of the story they say, "Shops stayed open later, and more customers stopped by on their way home." This shows how these bike lanes really gave more incentive to be outside and interacting with the local community.




	With this change in the community structure that included the new bike lanes parents and kids also found a benifit from this change. Parents let kids stay out longer in the afternoon beacuse of the increased trust. In the second paragraph of the story, "Parents said the streets felt calmer in the evening, and children could play outside for longer before dinner." This shows how the parents had more trust in the community even during darker or more unsafe hours. You can bring all of this back to how these bike lanes give more trust not just in families but in the community as a whole.




	 To sum up, these bike lanes did much more than just give a space on the street for bikers. These bike lanes gave a new view on the community as a whole while giving a space for people to walk. From kids biking to school to pedestrians stopping on their way home from work these bike lanes change the whole comminity. In conclusion, a simple thing like restructuring a road can really change a community as a whole.

questions.student_answer:
On the canary islands near the coast of africa there is a island that has a very special way of ancient comunication. In this small island community on La Gomera use a form a whisting to communicate to other villagers called El SIlibo. This language consits of a variation in pitches or lengthes of each whistle that can be herd up to two miles away. We dont know when this language first started but we know that they created it as a way to comunicate things like news, invitations and warnings. This language has been slowly disapering though the years but the spanish goverment is working to conserve it.




             La Gomera known for its grand valleys and steep clifs has on of the most special and unique local languages there has ever come to be. The small island community usees whistles with diffrent tones to comunicate messages across the island. While we dont know when this language was created we know that they used this language to communitcate messages to the whole island though the valleys and hills. The language consits of each vowel and consanant being convered into a sound that and be whistled and heard across the rugged landscape of the island. It has been used for centuries but has slowly started to fade.




         Around the 1980s less and less people were useing El silibo beacuse of the phone system. The Spanish government saw that the island was at risk of lousing this special language that was essential to keeping the culture alive. Now El silibo calsses are a required course in school. These classes teach students how to whistle and perfect their El Silibo skills. Some kids like Cyro prowdly whislte though the streets showing the pride in his ancestors.




        Even though El Silibo is taught in schools it is still not the most spoken language. El Silibo is most used for entertainment for tourists or at cultural events but it is still very important as to the people as they can demonstarte their heritage and pride for their ancestors. This can make this forgotten language feel more intigrated into the islands history and culture. This shows that even though it is no longer a useful language the local residents find ways of keeping their language alive.




          In conclusion El Slibo is a very important part of undersnading how cultures can evolve languages for special situations and occasions. Before phones El Silibo was more nessicary to know how to communicate though the island. In the end kids like Cyro will keep the legacy of their ancestors going on though generations and people will always we intertained and curious about El SIlibo.

questions.student_answer:
When you think of a lively community, you probably don't think of an abanonded parking lot. In many communities around the U.S. people have started projects converting abandoned lots into community gardens that benifit the community in many ways. These gardens provide fresh produce to a community which sometimes hard to find. These community spaces can bring people in the neighborhood together and gives safe place to meet new people. The enviorment also benifits from a community garden as plants absorb carbon dioxide and soil absorbs water to reduce runoff. There is many ways community gardens are helping communities so lets dive deeper in some examples.




 	You will find empty plots of land in neighborhoods all over the U.S., these places can feel sad and lifeless but a new project aims to give them new life. Gardeners and community members have started converting old land plots into community gardens as a shared space and place for people to contrubute and learn. In the 2nd paragraph of the passage they state ,"Neighbors work side by side to plant seeds water crops and care for the soil." As stated in the passage these places let all neighbors work together to a big common goal which brings the community closer. These gardens not only bring people together but it brings everyone together in good health.







	On a topic of good health many cities lack fresh produce because of food deserts. Communty gardens provide free accesible produce to the community that works hard on growing it. As stated in the 2nd paragraph of the passage, "for many families, fresh produce can be expensive or hard to find." This shows how people want produce but is is not so simple in parts of the U.S and these gardens help with that. These gardens not only help people thay healthy but also the envoirment.




 

	These community gardens also benifit the envoirment as plants and trees help with all sorts of envormental issues. Plants and trees absorb carbon dioxide from the air as there is lots of carbon dioxide in cities. The gardens also absorb water in the soil to reduce runoff. And as stated in the 5th paragraph of the passage, "They also give insecs and birds a place to live in crowded cities." Just one garden can give a handfull of benefits not just to all aspects of nature but the community too.







	In conclusion community gardens can help relive a dead plot of land in a community and make it beneficial for all. These gardens help the envoirment from reducing carbon dioxide and giving animals a place to live. They also creat fresh accesible produce for a whole community. All of this while bringing a community together in the procces creating new friends and better neighbor interactions. Finnaly every community should put in the time for one of these great gardens not just for them but for everyone.

questions.student_answer:
What would you find if you were to dig?
The correct answer is dirt, also know as soil, Soil is the scientific word for dirt.
Soil is everywhere, under grass, underwater and so many other places.
Thats why it covers most of earths land.
Soil creates life, such as plants, flowers, and fruits.
Soil is a food source for many animals and plants.
But they dont eat the accual soil itself, they eat the nutrients in it.
Many living being live in soil aswell, such as worms and groundhogs.
The cool part is, even we cant live without soil.
Plants need soil to survive and grow.
Without soil, there would be no plants, which mean no animals!
What is soil made of and what part do plants eat?
Soil exists of rocks, air, and water.
Soil also has dead plants and dead animals from when they died and rotted.
Now lets get to what plants eat.
When twigs and leaves fall, and tiny insects die, what do you think happens to them?
I bet you guessed they just stay there forever.
Well accually, they all rot and turn into black substance called humus.
Humus is food for the plants, unlike us, they like to eat all kinds of bugs and leaves.
Lets get to some different kinds of soil.
Some soils include Sandy soil, the sticky gross soil with includes high amounts of clay, fun fact, once this clay soil dires, it becomes as hard as concrete.
More soils include Soil with a lot of silt with evaporates after a while.
The question is now, what kind of soil is used for plants?
Its consists of sand and silt, but limits on clay.
it evens out the amount of air and water and includes much humus.
Now go ouside and dig again, tell me what kind of soil you find, and what kind of life you see.

questions.student_answer:
Imagine a camel walking around with boxes on it back. You would guess the boxes are full of food right? Well they're acctually full of books. This special sight is found near the "Camel Mobile Library" It is there to help people read and write. The camels walk those boxes of books all the the way to places like Garissa, where a lot of people own animals and enjoy moving alot. There are no nearby libraries in Garissa, so camels bring books to them. A librarian named Rashid Farah said "The people move alot. They are here today, but tormorrow they may be gone." Thats why the camels keep bringing them books so kids can continue learning. At most schools, the camel will kneel down infront of the Herders, and they will then unbox the books. Then a teacher places a tent down, students help put the books on the mats. Students take turns reading, and they enjoy it. Vehicles that move on the ground cant survive the rough terrain of Garissa. But camals have enough strength and energy to walk across all of the terrain. They carry food and medicine. Now they carry books too. Camels are trustworthy, so people trust them to carry the books around without dropping them. The camel library is also useful for the production of new books. Once, somebody named Alfred Muchilwa, wrote a book based on the journeys that camels take.

In the story, a camel named Gellow was delivering books, but a lion scares him and makes him drop the book. But then some children come and save the books and the camel. Most families that live in Garissa enjoy stories of daily life. The story of Gellow feels somewhat real to them. Reading is important, it helps us share ideas, communicate with other and learn about our planet. The camel library is building us, one camel at a time.

questions.student_answer:
For a long period of time, many people have played a game so called Pokémon.

The game originated from Satoshi Tajiri. he yearned of creating a game that was interesting and exciting.

As a child, Tajiri enjoyed insects. He would spend hours trying to catch one. He loved them so much his friends called him "Dr. bug."

He would always say, "Every new bug was a mystery." Collecting bug made him feel rewarded.

When he grew older, he enjoyed playing video games. He learned coding to make his own games. He thought most games were boring and not exciting enough.

 He wanted to make something everybody could enjoy. He remembered about his old insect collection and decided to use that as insperation.

He then created a game. In the game, players look for characters called Pokémon. There were over 150 Pokémon to collect.

Players threw Pokéballs at the little creatures and would catch them. Players could also trade with eachother.
 
The game had a slogan, and that was "Gotta catch 'em all!" For Tajiri, Pokémon were just like collecting bugs. He wished that players would feel the same happiness he felt as a kid.

The game became a very big thing, selling millions of copies. It then turned into a card game, an and app, and then a TV show. It even became a movie!

Tajiri turned a love for bugs, into an amazing game that to this day, is still popular.

questions.title: Essay with Plain Text
questions.prompt: Prompt In the passage "Dive into a Sunken Museum" by Gail Skroback Hennessey, readers learn about artist Jason deCaires Taylor's unusual underwater sculptures. Write  explaining why Jason chose to place his sculptures under the sea. a well-organized paragraph Your paragraph should: Make sure to: Write your paragraph in the box provided. clearly state your central idea organize your writing develop your ideas in detail use evidence from the selection in your response use correct spelling, capital
questions.student_answer:
An artist named Jason deCaires Taylor has created over 500 life-size statues. But these are not normal statues, they are under the sea!

Jason has created two statue parks under the Caribbean Sea. The first one has 65 statues, it's nearby Grenada. The other one, in Cancun, Mexico, has almost 500 statues. It holds the record for the largest underwater statue park ever.

If you want to see these amazing statues up close, you must bring scuba or snorkel gear. Or if you don't want to get wet, You can also take a glass-bottom boat.

Why make statues under the sea you ask? Jason wants to protect coral reefs. Every single year, many swimmers go under and visit the reefs. But when admiring them, they accidently hurt them without knowing it. So if people swin to the statues instead, the reefs will be safe.

A seven-year-old kid named Sam Clarke decided to visit the park in Grenada. 'I wore a mask and snorkel,' Sam said. 'On my feet I wore fins that helped me swim.'

Sam saw a lot of statues. His favorite was the Circle Of Children. It is twenty-six children including both boys and girls stand in a circle, Holding hands under the ocean.

If you take a look at the statues faces, you can spot that have their eyes closed. That is because the children who posed for the statues had to keep their eyes closed while Jason made the mold. It took two hours.

Not long after, they were put into the ocean. Soon after, ocean life began to take them over and climb onto the statues and cover them. Sponges and seaweed grew on them, and many fish started to visit. After a while, life took over the statues.

And was Jason bothered by the sea life covering his art? 'No,' Jason says. 'I like it most of all. Each visit is new, because the sea changes the art.'

Sam loved the trip so much! 'Snorkeling in the statue park was great,' Sam said. 'I saw fish, cool statues, and even a man on a bike!'

incorrect_questions.prompt: Prompt In the passage "Dive into a Sunken Museum" by Gail Skroback Hennessey, readers learn about artist Jason deCaires Taylor's unusual underwater sculptures. Write  explaining why Jason chose to place his sculptures under the sea. a well-organized paragraph Your paragraph should: Make sure to: Write your paragraph in the box provided. clearly state your central idea organize your writing develop your ideas in detail use evidence from the selection in your response use correct spelling, capital
incorrect_questions.student_answer:
An artist named Jason deCaires Taylor has created over 500 life-size statues. But these are not normal statues, they are under the sea!

Jason has created two statue parks under the Caribbean Sea. The first one has 65 statues, it's nearby Grenada. The other one, in Cancun, Mexico, has almost 500 statues. It holds the record for the largest underwater statue park ever.

If you want to see these amazing statues up close, you must bring scuba or snorkel gear. Or if you don't want to get wet, You can also take a glass-bottom boat.

Why make statues under the sea you ask? Jason wants to protect coral reefs. Every single year, many swimmers go under and visit the reefs. But when admiring them, they accidently hurt them without knowing it. So if people swin to the statues instead, the reefs will be safe.

A seven-year-old kid named Sam Clarke decided to visit the park in Grenada. 'I wore a mask and snorkel,' Sam said. 'On my feet I wore fins that helped me swim.'

Sam saw a lot of statues. His favorite was the Circle Of Children. It is twenty-six children including both boys and girls stand in a circle, Holding hands under the ocean.

If you take a look at the statues faces, you can spot that have their eyes closed. That is because the children who posed for the statues had to keep their eyes closed while Jason made the mold. It took two hours.

Not long after, they were put into the ocean. Soon after, ocean life began to take them over and climb onto the statues and cover them. Sponges and seaweed grew on them, and many fish started to visit. After a while, life took over the statues.

And was Jason bothered by the sea life covering his art? 'No,' Jason says. 'I like it most of all. Each visit is new, because the sea changes the art.'

Sam loved the trip so much! 'Snorkeling in the statue park was great,' Sam said. 'I saw fish, cool statues, and even a man on a bike!'

analysis.pattern_summary: Kingston shows a clear pattern of incomplete responses and fundamental writing mechanics issues that persist across all tests. Despite showing some ability with sentence combining and basic grammar concepts, he consistently leaves questions blank, provides incomplete answers, and struggles with paragraph development and text evidence integration.
analysis.skill_gaps: sentence completion, paragraph development, text evidence integration, appositive construction, response completion strategies, writing stamina
analysis.alphawrite_vs_test: There's a significant disconnect where AlphaWrite shows "MASTERED" status for skills Kingston clearly hasn't mastered on actual tests, particularly combining sentences with appositives and paragraph writing from prompts. The AlphaWrite data appears unreliable or the student may be getting external help during practice.
analysis.rushing_impact: Rushing significantly impacted performance on tests G3.4, G3.5, G3.6, and G3.7, where he left multiple questions completely blank, suggesting time management and task completion are major barriers.
analysis.recommended_activities: Write Freeform Paragraph (Paragraphs G3): student needs intensive practice completing full responses rather than partial sentences. Combine Sentences With Appositives (Production G3): student consistently fails appositive questions despite "mastered" status. Write Paragraph From Prompt (Paragraph From Prompt G3): student struggles with developing complete paragraphs with supporting details. Fragment Or Sentence (To Sentence G3): student needs reinforcement on sentence completion. Turn Outline Into Draft (Paragraphs G3): student needs scaffolding to complete longer written responses.

questions.student_answer: To this day, there are many modern sports: football, basketball, soccer, and so on. If we go back in time to the 1700s, in Britian, we will see the first sports being made. In the 1700s, games like golf and cricket were played among the rich, partly because they had more free time and more money. Then came the rules. questions.student_answer:
Have you ever wondered how students learn new languages in effective ways? Students learn languages in many ways.




They can learn a new language by having the teacher use the new language for every word he or she says. First, the kids learn that new language by listening to that language the teacher says and repeats it. Furthermore, it can be used for simple requests like asking to go to the bathroom. In summary, children can learn a new language through immersion.




They can also learn a new language by using real communication. First, the teacher can call a students friend who speaks a different language , so that they can learn it. Last, some experts believe that when you are younger, you can learn a language faster. 




In conclusion, there are many ways children can learn a language, and there is no better or worse way.

In conclusion, getting sleep is very important because it help you fight germs and remember things.
